newsitem.title: UK: Racal drops sharply after profit warning.
newsitem.headline: Racal drops sharply after profit warning.

text.p: Shares in Racal Electronics Plc tumbled on Friday, after the defence electronics and communications group warned of a loss in its Data Products group.
The stock was down 33p at 244 by 1137 GMT in volume of 440,311 shares, after falling as low as 240p -- its lowest for four months.
The company said the Data Products group "has regrettably not achieved the modest profit expected in the second half" and would incur a loss of abour seven million stg.

Analyst Justinian Clifford-Bowles at Credit Lyonnais Laing said the statement was an obvious disappointment but pointed out that the company's target of returning a division which lost 12 million stg in the first half to profit was "somewhat ambitious."

However, he said the statement did not affect the key issues for the stock, which remained the relatively poor level of profitability of the group -- and the expectation that Chairman Sir Ernest Harrison will take measures to boost shareholder returns in his last year at the company.
"They are not making an adequate return on sales," the Laing analyst said, "and this is just going to put more pressure on Harrison to increase value for shareholders."
